newsitem.title: USA: Parts of Illinois River still shut -- US Coast Guard.
newsitem.headline: Parts of Illinois River still shut -- US Coast Guard.

text.p: Three stretches of the Illinois River remained closed to navigation Friday due to high water, a U.S. Coast Guard official said.
"At this time, they show to be closed," Petty Officer Kenneth Bellino with the U.S. Coast Guard Marine Safety Office in St. Louis said.

The areas of the Illinois closed to river traffic were River Mile 127 to 128 (Liverpool, Ill.), River Mile 140 to 144 (Illinois Department Conservation Banner Marsh area), and River Mile 166 to 182 (North Peoria to Henry, Ill.), river officials said.
Bellino said U.S. Coast Guard officials will reassess the situation later Friday morning to determine if the three areas will remain closed to navigation.
The stretches of river were closed Wednesday to protect houses and properties in low-lying areas.
The closures have stranded "a small number of barges" north of Peoria, Ill., said Mike Zerbonia, chief of the maintenance section of the Army Corps of Engineers in Peoria.
River officials plan to run a test barge through some of the flooded areas Friday to if the vessel's wake affects the houses, Zerbonia said..
Based on Thursday's weather data, the Illinois River at Peoria, Ill., is projected to crest Monday at 26 feet, and the river currently is at 25.6 feet, Zerbonia said.
More rain is forecast for Illinois Friday night and Saturday, which could aggravate the current high-water situation, Zerbonia said.
Most of Illinois has been assigned a 70 to 80 percent probability of rain on both days before clearing occurs on Sunday, according to a forecast from Weather Express of Omaha, Neb.
The high water levels and swift currents were making loading barges very difficult, cash grain merchandisers said.
